subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for legacy ownerless session rows, with recovery limited to operator/non-plugin management or a provenance-safe migration?
rationale: Strict rejection preserves plugin isolation but intentionally changes persisted upgrade behavior, while allowing the caller to adopt an ownerless row would retain compatibility by weakening the authorization boundary.

options.title: Strict runtime with recovery guidance
options.body: Reject ownerless plugin-runtime patches and document a clear operator or non-plugin recovery path.

options.title: Add provenance-safe migration
options.body: Keep runtime enforcement strict and assign ownership only where historical plugin provenance can be established safely.

options.title: Permit caller adoption
options.body: Allow a plugin-runtime caller to claim an ownerless row, preserving access but weakening cross-plugin isolation.

recommendation.title: Strict runtime with recovery guidance
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless plugin-runtime patches and document a clear operator or non-plugin recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows the strongest available ownership of gateway session behavior and associated product-boundary decisions.
